text.tspan: Figure 9: The screen picked the analogue ensemble on these months, so
its 0.23-point gain is biased upward

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each fitted arm's mean absolute error minus B0's over the first 10 of the 18 scored months, in percentage points of capacity; negative beats B0. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% confidence interval of the paired difference from resampling whole months and a seed. Only AN clearly beat B0, and 6 arms clearly lost to it. A screen, not a test: it picks an arm for the later months. Green: the confidence interval is below zero. Orange: above zero. Grey: it includes zero. Bottom: R4 and R5 on CRPS, the continuous ranked probability score, which compares the whole forecast distribution with the measured power. Each is drawn beside B0 on the same rows.'

text.aria-label: Title text 'Without the plant-month with the largest B0 error (one plant in one month), AN's difference is -0.21 points, 95% confidence interval [-0.38, -0.06]. The no-fit arms are not paired with B0. Their mean absolute errors, against B0's 9.2%: R1s 9.1%, R4 9.2%, R2 9.6%, climatology 14.8%, diurnal_persistence 16.5%, persistence 26.1%. Lead-day 1 is the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. Out-of-fold means each forecast is made by a model that never trained on that month. The fitted arms use three training runs (seeds); the CRPS panel uses one. The screening losses are exploratory; this paired analysis is post hoc, written after the first run's results were known. With 17 rows, about 1 could reach significance at the 5% level by chance. Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, the forecast clear-sky index and the spread of the power (rescaled by the Haurwitz clear-sky model's irradiance) on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. Q30: the 30-day 90th percentile and median of power at the same hour. W7 (the weekly statistics): the minimum, maximum, and mean of power at the same hour over the last 7 whole days. PC (the satellite ratio): the 7-day ratio of power to the satellite irradiance of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS; all-sky global horizontal irradiance, hourly, from Meteosat Second Generation), and the 30-day ratio of CAMS to forecast irradiance. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance (the transfer ratio). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). T1: days since the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides; its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. N2: a random day from months not being scored (a null control). L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3, and RP together. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. RP: the plant's recent energy relative to the other plants. S2: a two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. CTX7: seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. S3: a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days. R4: B0 clamped at the plant's clipping ceiling, with no fit. R5: B0 plus recent residual quantiles, with no fit.'
text.tspan: Without the plant-month with the largest B0 error (one plant in one month), AN's difference is -0.21 points, 95% confidence
The no-fit arms are not paired with B0. Their mean absolute errors, against B0's 9.2%: R1s 9.1%, R4 9.2%, R2 9.6%,
climatology 14.8%, diurnal_persistence 16.5%, persistence 26.1%.
Lead-day 1 is the forecast for the day after the day it is issued. Out-of-fold means each forecast is made by a model that
never trained on that month. The fitted arms use three training runs (seeds); the CRPS panel uses one.
The screening losses are exploratory; this paired analysis is post hoc, written after the first run's results were known.
With 17 rows, about 1 could reach significance at the 5% level by chance.
Arms. AN: the analogue ensemble: the mean, the forecast clear-sky index and the spread of the power (rescaled by the Haurwitz
clear-sky model's irradiance) on the 5 of the last 30 days whose forecast clear-sky index was closest to the target's. Q30:
the 30-day 90th percentile and median of power at the same hour. W7 (the weekly statistics): the minimum, maximum, and mean
of power at the same hour over the last 7 whole days. PC (the satellite ratio): the 7-day ratio of power to the satellite
irradiance of the Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS; all-sky global horizontal irradiance, hourly, from Meteosat
Second Generation), and the 30-day ratio of CAMS to forecast irradiance. TF: the 30-day ratio of power to forecast irradiance
(the transfer ratio). N1: a random day 8 to 28 days earlier (keeps the plant's slowly changing output level). T1: days since
the record began. Month-block folds interleave, so trees can interpolate a scored month's level from months on both sides;
its gain is what interpolation buys, never drift a live forecast could use. IM: the morning's power on the forecast day. N2:
a random day from months not being scored (a null control). L1: B0 plus the power at the same hour on the latest whole day
before the forecast was issued (two days before the target day for a day-ahead forecast). KS: all of L1, IM, W7, Q30, TF, S3,
and RP together. L2: L1 plus that hour's weather forecast. RP: the plant's recent energy relative to the other plants. S2: a
two-step forecast that adds a first-stage forecast and its residual at the lag hour. CK: the plant's clipping ceiling. CTX7:
seven separate daily lags and their weather forecasts. S3: a two-step forecast that adds the first-stage forecast's mean
residual over the last 1, 7, and 30 days. R4: B0 clamped at the plant's clipping ceiling, with no fit. R5: B0 plus recent
residual quantiles, with no fit.
